canonical.title: Floyd-Warshall — All-Pairs Shortest Distances
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/4. Shortest Path Problems/09. Floyd Warshall Algorithm.cpp

narrative.title: The Full Fare Chart Reconciliation
narrative.scenario: A rail company stores its fare table as a square grid: cell (i, j) is the direct fare from platform i to platform j, and a blank (-1) means no direct train. The revenue team must upgrade the table into a true cheapest-fare chart — every pair, via any connections — leaving blanks only where no sequence of trains connects the pair at all.
narrative.inputFormat: An n x n matrix where Matrix[i][j] is the direct edge weight from i to j, or -1 if no such edge exists.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the updated matrix holding the shortest distance for every ordered pair, with -1 restored where no path exists.
constraints: The graph is directed; Matrix[i][i] is 0

testCases.explanation: No connection improves any direct fare, and the blank stays blank.
Connections surface: 0->2 costs 5 via 1, 1->0 costs 3 via 2, and 2->1 costs 4 via 0.

hintLevels: Level 1: Ask for every pair: would hopping through one extra platform ever be cheaper?
Level 2: Fix the intermediate platform k, then relax every pair (i, j) through it; repeat for all k.
Level 3: Swap -1 for a huge sentinel before relaxing and restore -1 afterwards so blanks never look like real fares.
